title: HTTPS over Wi-Fi: fetching and sending data

spans.text: An ESP32 can join a router in STA mode to fetch information from a service or send sensor readings to it.
HTTP GET retrieves a response; POST sends data. HTTPS encrypts the exchange with TLS and authenticates the server certificate. Arduino-ESP32 provides

. Connect to Wi-Fi first, trust the correct CA certificate, check status codes, bound response sizes, and close each request.

Sending data to a remote internet service does not require opening an inbound router port: outbound HTTPS or MQTT works behind NAT. If a local device server must be reachable remotely, use an authenticated HTTPS gateway/tunnel rather than casually forwarding a device port.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Provide the CA certificate that validates your service; do not disable certificate checks. `api.example.org` is a placeholder. The raw `WiFiClient` example uses unencrypted HTTP, so never send secrets through it. Call requests after Wi-Fi connects and keep credentials out of source control.
